Quick update from the infra side — initial evidence points to a transient proxy egress issue on our primary peering cluster. Observed:
- Increase in DNS resolution latencies to several upstream resolvers (100–600ms spikes) starting ~08:34 UTC.
- Proxy pool returning 502s for ~4% of requests (patterned by client IP ranges).
- One of the egress NAT nodes shows conntrack approaching 95% for a 30-minute window; we saw ephemeral SYN retries.

Subject: Incident mitigation summary — Mercury Retail (resolved)

Summary (short):
- Root cause (interim): partial egress path degradation combined with elevated conntrack on a NAT cluster; secondary effect was increased DNS latency to a set of upstream resolvers which pushed some flows to a slower/proxy path returning intermittent 502s.
- Mitigation performed (08:55–10:15 UTC):
  1) Temporarily pinned Mercury egress to alternate peering cluster (bypassed saturating transit)
  2) Cleared conntrack on affected NAT nodes and increased conntrack timers for short-lived flows
  3) Adjusted proxy ACLs to accept previously blocked backend routable ranges (removed a stale deny rule)
- Outcome: 5xx rate reduced from ~4% to 0.2% within 20 minutes; latency returned to baseline in ~40 minutes.

Next steps:
- Post-mortem scheduled tomorrow 09:00 PT — draft attached.
- Follow-up: permanent peering failover tests, conntrack autoscaling threshold raised, and a short TTL DNS test plan.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-0804.md
